summary:
--- PART 1/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice emphasizes cooperation, forgiveness, repair. But objective is maximize cumulative score, so exploitation may pay off if opponent is unconditionally cooperative."
STRATEGY: Parent slot 3 is an adaptive IPD strategy that starts cooperatively, waits ~10 rounds, then defects if opponent defection rate is high and cooperates/punishes if low. The trace simulates matches against always-C, always-D, TFT, forgiving TFT, random, and Grim, and plans changes: probe early with D at rounds 2–3, exploit unconditional cooperators by defecting forever, otherwise use forgiving TFT and defect on the final round.

--- PART 2/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the general advice, we should be forgiving." and "The general advice says start cooperatively."
STRATEGY: Parent waits 10 rounds before exploiting unconditional cooperators; trace simulates TFT/forgiving-TFT/always-D opponents and designs a faster probe (C, D, D) with retaliation detection, then a forgiving cooperative mode that defects only after two consecutive opponent defections and defects on the final round.

--- PART 3/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice strongly emphasizes forgiveness and avoiding permanent retaliation. Our strategy does forgive, but against Grim Trigger, it can't restore cooperation because Grim never forgives."
STRATEGY: Parent starts C for first 10 rounds, then switches to high-defection mode if opponent defection rate exceeds 0.6, with occasional C every 10 rounds. Simulated against always-C, TFT-like, forgiving TFT, Grim Trigger, and parent. Changed cooperative mode to defect after two consecutive opponent defections, and considered adding a break-out rule after long mutual defection.

--- PART 4/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So our modified strategy with the "break DD after 5 consecutive D's" successfully escapes the DD trap against parent!" and "The modification to break DD after 5 consecutive D's works beautifully."
STRATEGY: Parent is a conditional strategy that defects heavily when our defection rate is high, then switches to a moderate TFT-like mode. The trace simulates our strategy against this parent and against TFT/always-C/always-D. It changes our cooperative-mode rule to return C after 5 consecutive opponent defections, breaking the DD trap and restoring mutual cooperation.
